fields.meta_title: Training Request Form Builder With Routing | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a training request form that checks allowances and training records, then routes each request to the person who decides. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Training Request Form That Routes Every Request
fields.hero_description: Describe who asks for training and who says yes. Emergent builds the training request form, the approval steps and a table of every request, ready to share.
fields.features_subheading: A blank template stops at the signature line. These pieces handle the checks a coordinator usually does by email.
fields.feature_1:
Course details and a business case

Ask for the course, the provider and the cost, then a short case for how it helps the job. Managers read the request and its reason on one screen before they approve or return it.
fields.feature_2:
Allowance balance on each request

Link every employee to a yearly development allowance. The form shows the approver what is left, and any course priced above the balance picks up a second approver from finance.
fields.feature_3:
Requests to your trainers, pooled

Take requests from members or branches who want your staff to teach. Count them by topic and region, and alert the coordinator once enough arrive to justify one shared class.
fields.feature_4:
Attendees checked against the log

Look up each named attendee in your training records before seats are booked. Anyone with a current completion is left off the list, and the class fills with people who need it.
fields.feature_5:
Preferred dates matched to trainers

Let the requester rank a few dates that suit them. The app holds those against your trainers' calendars, confirms the first open one and emails the requester the time and room.
fields.feature_6:
Export the code to your repo

Move the whole training request app to your GitHub repository whenever IT wants it in-house. The request table travels with it, along with every approval and the name behind it.

fields.tab_content_1:
Finance co-signs any course over the allowance

Corvane Freight gives every employee $1,500 a year for outside learning. Dana Kim, an analyst, asks for a $1,295 analytics certificate with $900 of her allowance left. Her manager approves the business case. Because the course runs $395 past her balance, the request then goes to the finance director, Marcus Bell.
fields.tab_content_2:
Six valve requests turn into one regional class

The Mesa Valley Water Partnership sends trainers to small water systems that ask. Each request names the topic and the crew size. Once 6 systems in the northern district had asked for valve exercising, a post in the training team's Slack channel had the coordinator book one regional class instead of separate visits.
fields.tab_content_3:
Lapsed records decide who gets a lockout seat

OSHA requires lockout training for anyone who services the equipment, and Kestrel Foods repeats it every 12 months. A supervisor requests seats for 4 technicians. The form checks each name against the training log. Two are still current. Luis Ortega and Dee Brooks get the seats in the next session.
fields.tab_content_4:
Three dates offered, the second one confirmed

Granite Ridge's tech team trains school staff on request. Lincoln Elementary asks for a gradebook session for 14 teachers and offers three after-school dates. Tuesday falls on a day the trainers are fully booked. Wednesday is open. The app books a trainer for it and emails the principal the room and start time.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Training Request Form
fields.howto_description: Two questions shape most of the form: who is asking for training, and who pays for it. Answer both before you write the prompt.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Find out which way requests travel
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Describe the form in a prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide whether employees are asking to attend training or outside groups are asking your team to teach it. The first kind needs a cost and an approver. The second needs proposed dates and a headcount. One app can hold a form for each.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Note where the money comes from, such as a department budget or a yearly allowance per person. Name the approver for each case by role, not by name. Settle with finance now how far over an allowance a request may go before they sign.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Put the course and its cost near the top, then the business case in the requester's own words. Keep the case to one or two questions, such as which task the training improves. Specific answers get decided faster than long essays.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Tell Emergent who requests training, who approves it and what the form should check. Emergent builds the training request form, the approval steps and a requests table in a database you own. Change any rule later by describing the change in the same chat.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Connect the spreadsheet or HR system that holds completion records. The form can then flag attendees who already hold a current completion and leave them off, instead of a coordinator checking each name by hand after the request arrives.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Write the message an approved request sends and the one for a request returned for more detail. Pick email or Slack for each. A requester who can see the status stops chasing their manager, and every decision stays on the request record.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before launch, file one request that fits every rule and one that breaks a rule, such as a course priced over the allowance. Check that each reaches the right approver and that both land in the requests table with their decisions recorded.

plan.angle: The live top 10 splits two ways. Template.net, Jotform's training funds template and a Howland reference page offer the employee version: ask to attend a course, justify it, get a signature. The Pennsylvania Office of Open Records, Tulane's research office and an Arizona rural water association post the other version: ask an organization to come and teach, with dates offered and notice required. Google's AI Overview lists the sections a request should hold. Every result stops at the blank fields. This page covers both directions and shows what happens after submit: a course priced against what is left of an allowance, requests on one topic pooled into a regional class, seats booked only for people whose training record has lapsed, and a session confirmed on the first date a trainer is free. The FAQ answers the People Also Ask questions on writing, emailing and replying to a request.
tab_stories: A Corvane Freight analyst asks for a $1,295 analytics certificate with $900 of her development allowance left, so the $395 gap adds the finance director as a second approver after her manager.

Members of the Mesa Valley Water Partnership ask the partnership to teach valve exercising, and once 6 systems in the northern district have asked, a message in the training team's Slack channel asks the coordinator to schedule one regional class instead of separate visits.

A Kestrel Foods maintenance supervisor asks for lockout training for 4 technicians, the form checks the training log, finds 2 trained within the plant's 12-month window and books seats for Luis Ortega and Dee Brooks.

Lincoln Elementary asks the Granite Ridge district tech team to train 14 teachers on the new gradebook, offers three dates, and the request is confirmed for the second one because that is the first day a trainer is free.
